words.gloss: together with; kulattha (horse gram, Macrotyloma uniflorum; standard)
fruit (phala); sauvīraka (a sour fermented gruel, usually of barley; standard); joined with

hindi: कुलत्थ यानी कुलथी के साथ, उबाला हुआ मस्तु यानी दही का पानी, फल और सौवीरक यानी खट्टी कांजी से युक्त।
english: With kulattha (horse gram), boiled mastu (curd-water, whey), with (ones) joined with phala (fruit) and sauvīraka (a sour fermented gruel).
notes: GROUPING: 83 and 84 read as one sentence with 82 (the instrumental list at the end of 82 is carried over); the verb is āsthāpayet in 84, so this unit has no verb. 'phala' is not specified in the text (no identification made). The instrumental plurals of 83 are read loosely with the items of 82 and 84; the exact attachment is uncertain.

words.gloss: should give an āsthāpana (decoction enema; standard)
with rock salt (sindhūttha, lit. 'arisen from Sindhu'; standard)

hindi: सेंधा नमकों के साथ आस्थापन करे, जाङ्गल रसों से भोजन किए हुए को।
english: He should give an āsthāpana (decoction enema) with rock salt (sindhūttha), to (one) who has eaten with jāṅgala (dry-country) juices (rasa).
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 83 (āsthāpayet governs the items of 83). 'aśitam' is read as the person (accusative), 'one who has eaten'. 'jāṅgala rasa' is literally the juices of dry-country (animals); the tradition takes these as meat soups, but the text does not say so. 'sindhūtthaiḥ' is plural as printed (rock salts); kept as printed.

words.gloss: unclear (printed 'dhanya': 'fortunate, wealthy', or a damaged form)
should give an anuvāsana (oil enema; standard)

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार, वात को जीतने वाले धन्य, जिसका अर्थ अस्पष्ट है, के साथ भली-भाँति पकाए गए तेल से अनुवासन करे।
english: On a conjectural reading: he should give an anuvāsana (oil enema) with oil well cooked with the Vāta-conquering (anilajit, lit. wind-conquering) dhanya (unclear).

text_flags.why: possible: 'vipakka' is a misprint of 'vipakva' (kva read as kka)

notes: The sense of 'anilajiddhanya' is doubtful. 'anilajit' (Vāta-conquering) probably describes the drugs the oil is cooked with; 'dhanya' as printed gives no clear sense (it could be a damaged form of dravya 'drug' or dhānya 'grain'); no reading is applied. 'vipakka' is printed with kk; kept as printed, vipakva is read.

words.gram: pres. part. nir-√hṛ, m. nom. sg.

hindi: कोमल कोष्ठ वाले में, दुर्बल में, बहुत तीक्ष्ण और अत्यधिक बाहर निकालने वाली बस्ति
english: In (one) with a soft koṣṭha (belly), in the weak (one), a basti (enema) that is very sharp and over-expelling,
notes: GROUPING: 86 and 87 appear to be one sentence (the verb 'kuryāt' is in 87). Printed 'nirharan' is read as the present participle of nir-√hṛ, 'expelling'. The list 'mṛdukoṣṭhe abale' is two locatives; the persons are not named in the Sanskrit.

hindi: हिचकी कर दे। उसमें जो हिचकी को नष्ट करने वाला और बृंहण यानी पुष्टि देने वाला हो, वह हितकारी है।
english: (it) would cause hiccup (hidhmā). In that (case), whatever is hiccup-destroying and nourishing (bṛṃhaṇa) is beneficial.
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 86; the subject of 'kuryāt' is the basti of 86. Hidhmā = hiccup (standard).
lines_deva: कुर्याद्धिध्मां हितं तत्र हिध्माघ्नं बृंहणं च यत्
lines_iast: kuryāddhidhmāṃ hitaṃ tatra hidhmāghnaṃ bṛṃhaṇaṃ ca yat

words.gloss: balā (probably Sida cordifolia; probable); sthirā (disputed: often śālaparṇī, Desmodium gangeticum); and the rest (ādi); kāśmarya (Gmelina arborea; standard); triphalā (the three myrobalans: harītakī, Terminalia chebula; bibhītaka, Terminalia bellirica; āmalaka, Phyllanthus emblica; standard); juices (rasa)

hindi: बला यानी सम्भवतः बरियार, स्थिरा यानी सम्भवतः सरिवन और अन्य, काश्मर्य यानी गम्हार और त्रिफला यानी हरड़, बहेड़ा और आँवला के रसों के साथ, सेंधा नमकों के साथ
english: With the juices (rasa) of balā (probably Sida cordifolia), sthirā (identity disputed; perhaps śālaparṇī, Desmodium gangeticum) and the rest, kāśmarya (Gmelina arborea) and triphalā (the three myrobalans), and with rock salts (saindhava),

text_flags.why: possible: anusvāra printed for visarga and the space between rasaiḥ and saindhavaiḥ is missing

notes: GROUPING: 88 and 89 appear to be one sentence (the verb 'anuvāsayet' is in 89). Identifications: balā = Sida cordifolia (probable; several Sida species are called balā); sthirā = disputed (often śālaparṇī, Desmodium gangeticum, but other plants carry the name); kāśmarya = Gmelina arborea (standard); triphalā = harītakī, bibhītaka, āmalaka (standard). 'ādi' is read 'and the rest' after balā and sthirā. The printed 'rasaiṃ saiṃdhavaiḥ' has anusvāra for visarga and no space; see text_flags.

words.gloss: together with; prasannā (the clear upper layer of surā liquor; standard); āranāla (sour fermented gruel, kāñjika; standard); sour (ones)

hindi: प्रसन्ना यानी सुरा का निथरा ऊपरी भाग, आरनाल यानी खट्टी कांजी और खट्टों के साथ तेल पकाकर अनुवासन करे।
english: Having cooked oil with prasannā (the clear upper layer of surā liquor), āranāla (a sour fermented gruel) and sour (ones), he should give an anuvāsana (oil enema).

text_flags.why: possible: 'pakvā' for paktvā (t lost; gerund of √pac); alternative: 'pakvam' agreeing with tailam, same sense

notes: GROUPING: appears to complete 88. 'pakvā' (printed) is taken as a gerund 'having cooked' (the usual gerund is paktvā); kept as printed. Surā is an intoxicating fermented drink.

hindi: गर्म जल और पिप्पली यानी पीपर से सना हुआ, नमक से युक्त, दे।
english: He should give (it) smeared (mixed) with hot water and with pippalī (long pepper), joined with salt.
notes: The object of 'dadyāt' is not stated; 'aktam' and 'saṃyutam' are neuter accusatives agreeing with an unstated neuter noun (probably the oil or enema of 89), not applied.

words.gloss: smoke (dhūma); linctus (leha: something licked); juice (rasa); milk; sweating, fomentation (sveda)

hindi: धूम यानी धुआँ, लेह यानी चाटना, रस, दूध और स्वेद यानी सेंक से, और भोजन भी जो वात को दूर करने वाला हो।
english: With smoke (dhūma), linctus (leha), juice (rasa), milk and fomentation (sveda), and also food that drives away Vāta.
notes: The verb is carried over from 90 ('dadyāt' / 'should apply'); none is supplied. 'dhūma' = smoke (a medicated smoke is the usual practice, not stated here). 'annam' is accusative and 'vātanut' is read as agreeing with it.

hindi: बहुत तीक्ष्ण, या वात यानी वायु सहित, या ठीक से दबाया न गया
english: (A basti) that is very sharp, or with vāta (wind, air), or not properly pressed,
notes: GROUPING: 92 and 93 appear to be one sentence; the subject 'bastiḥ' is in 93. 'savāta' may mean 'with air (in the bag or syringe)' or 'with Vāta (the humour)'; the text does not say; both are possible.
lines_deva: अतितीक्ष्णः सवातो वा न वा सम्यक्प्रपीडितः
lines_iast: atitīkṣṇaḥ savāto vā na vā samyakprapīḍitaḥ

words.gloss: kāśa (Saccharum spontaneum; standard); kuśa (Desmostachya bipinnata; standard); utkaṭa (unclear here: 'excessive, strong', or a drug name)

hindi: बस्ति हृदय पर आघात करे। उसमें काश यानी काँस, कुश यानी कुशा घास और उत्कट, जिसका अर्थ यहाँ अस्पष्ट है, के साथ
english: The basti (enema) would strike the heart. In that (case), with kāśa (Saccharum spontaneum), kuśa (Desmostachya bipinnata) and utkaṭa (unclear),
notes: GROUPING: 93 to 95 read as one passage. 'utkaṭa' is unclear: it may be an adjective ('strong, excessive') or a drug name; no reading is applied and no identification is made. The sentence continues in 94 and 95.

words.gloss: together with; sour (ones); salt; skandha (trunk, stem; what is meant is unclear); karīra (bamboo shoot or Capparis decidua; disputed); badarī (jujube, Ziziphus jujuba; standard); fruits

hindi: सहित खट्टे, नमक, स्कन्ध यानी तना, जिसका आशय यहाँ अस्पष्ट है, करीर यानी बाँस का अंकुर या कैर और बदरी यानी बेर के फलों के साथ हो।
english: It would be with sour (ones), salt, skandha (trunk; unclear here), karīra (disputed: bamboo shoot, or the shrub Capparis decidua) and badarī (jujube) fruits,
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 93 and leads into 95 ('śṛtaiḥ'). The grouping of the compound is uncertain: 'sāmla' may attach only to 'lavaṇa' (with sour and salt), and 'skandha' may be a plant part rather than a drug. 'karīra' is disputed (bamboo shoot, or the thorny shrub Capparis decidua).

hindi: उबाले हुओं से बस्ति हितकारी है, पकाया हुआ, और वात को नष्ट करने वाले अनुवासनों से।
english: A basti with boiled (ones) is beneficial, siddha (cooked), and with Vāta-destroying anuvāsanas (oil enemas).
notes: GROUPING: appears to end the passage of 93 to 95. The syntax is loose: 'siddhaḥ' may mean 'cooked', 'accomplished' or 'effective', and 'vātaghnaiś cānuvāsanaiḥ' may belong with 'siddhaḥ' or be a second means; the translation keeps the order of the Sanskrit.

hindi: कोमल कोष्ठ वाले और अल्प दोष वाले के लिए, रूखी, तीक्ष्ण और अत्यधिक मात्रा वाली
english: For (one) with a soft koṣṭha (belly) and little doṣa, (a basti that is) dry, sharp and excessive in quantity,
notes: GROUPING: 96 to 98 appear to be one sentence; the subject (a basti) is understood from the context and the verb 'prakopayet' is in 97. 'atimātraka' is read 'exceeding the measure, excessive in quantity'. 'mṛdukoṣṭhālpadoṣasya' is read as one bahuvrīhi (soft koṣṭha, little doṣa), or as two genitives.

hindi: बस्ति के मलों को शीघ्र नष्ट करके वात और पित्त को कुपित कर दे।
english: having quickly destroyed the malas (wastes) of the basti, would aggravate Vāta and Pitta.
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 96. 'bastimalān' is printed with ḻ (ळ); read as mala. 'basti' can mean the enema or the bladder, and 98 lists 'basti' beside the navel and the anus, so 'bastimala' may be the wastes of the basti region or of the bladder; the translation keeps the word basti.

words.gloss: navel; basti (bladder, or the lower belly); anus

hindi: वे तो इसकी नाभि, बस्ति और गुदा को बार-बार काटते हुए
english: They, indeed, cutting his navel, basti (probably the bladder) and anus again and again,
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 97; 'te' is read as the two, Vāta and Pitta (dual neuter in 97, but 'te ... kṛntantaḥ' is plural masculine as printed). The sentence continues in 99. 'basti' between navel and anus is probably the bladder; this is not certain.

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार, विवर्ण यानी रंग का बिगड़ना, थोड़ा थोड़ा उत्थान यानी उठना; बस्ति निर्लेखन यानी खुरचने वाली हो।
english: On a conjectural reading: discolouration, a little-by-little arising (utthāna); the basti would be scraping (nirlekhana).

text_flags.why: possible: 'alapam' is a misreading of 'alpam' (lp for lap)

notes: The first token is damaged: 'vivarṇālpālapamutthānaṃ' is kept as printed; 'alapam' is probably 'alpam' (conjunct lp misread as lap). What 'utthāna' refers to is unclear (arising of the symptom, or of the stool). The reading is conjectural and no firm sense is built on it. 'nirlekhana' = scraping.

words.gloss: ikṣu (sugarcane, Saccharum officinarum; standard); and the rest

hindi: वहाँ मीठी और ठण्डी औषधियों से, और ईख यानी गन्ना आदि के साथ उबाला हुआ दूध
english: In that (case), with sweet and cool drugs (auṣadha), and milk boiled with sugarcane (ikṣu) and the rest,
notes: GROUPING: 100 and 101 appear to be one sentence; the verb is 'syāt' in 101. The words 'svādu śīta' are read as two adjectives of 'auṣadhaiḥ'.

words.gloss: yaṣṭyāhva (licorice, Glycyrrhiza glabra; standard); sesame (tila, Sesamum indicum; standard); pastes (kalka)

hindi: यष्ट्याह्व यानी मुलेठी और तिल के कल्कों से, दूध का भोजन करने वाले के लिए बस्ति हो।
english: With the pastes (kalka) of yaṣṭyāhva (licorice) and tila (sesame), a basti would be for (one) who eats milk.

text_flags.why: possible: 'vha' is a reversal of 'hva' (yaṣṭyāhva, licorice)

notes: GROUPING: appears to complete 100. The printed 'yaṣṭyāvha' has v and h reversed; yaṣṭyāhva ('named yaṣṭi') is read. 'kṣīrabhojinaḥ' is a genitive: 'of (one) who lives on milk'.

words.gloss: equal; sarja-rasa (resin of sarja, probably the sal tree, Shorea robusta; probable); yaṣṭyāhva (licorice)
jiṅgiṇī (Lannea coromandelica; probable); mud (kardama); añjana (collyrium; kind unclear)

hindi: बराबर सर्जरस यानी सम्भवतः राल, यष्ट्याह्व यानी मुलेठी, जिंगिनी यानी सम्भवतः झिंगन, कर्दम यानी कीचड़ और अञ्जन, जिसका प्रकार अस्पष्ट है
english: Equal sarja-rasa (probably the resin of the sal tree), yaṣṭyāhva (licorice), jiṅgiṇī (probably Lannea coromandelica), kardama (mud) and añjana (collyrium; kind unclear),

text_flags.why: possible: 'vha' is a reversal of 'hva' (as in 101)

notes: GROUPING: 102 and 103 appear to be one sentence ('vinīya' is in 103). 'sama' is read as 'equal' for the whole list. The printed 'yaṣṭyāvhaṃ' again reverses hva (see 101); 'karddama' (doubled dd) is read kardama. 'kardama' (mud, clay) as a drug is unusual; read literally. 'añjana' could be a pigment or collyrium; not narrowed.

hindi: दूध में डालकर, स्पष्ट खट्टे रस का भोजन करने वाले के लिए बस्ति हो।
english: Having put (these) into milk, a basti would be for (one) who eats a distinctly sour taste (rasa).
notes: GROUPING: appears to complete 102. 'vinīya' is read 'having put in, having added' (the items of 102 into milk). 'vyaktāmlarasabhojinaḥ' is read literally as 'eating a clear sour taste'; the text does not say what food is meant.

hindi: चिपचिपी बस्ति हितकारी है, और मीठों के साथ उबाला हुआ स्नेह यानी तेल या वसा।
english: A slimy (picchila) basti is beneficial, and a sneha (oil or fat) boiled with sweet (ones).
notes: The word order is 'picchilaś ca hito bastiḥ snehaś ca madhuraiḥ śṛtaḥ'; 'hitaḥ' is carried to the second clause. 'madhuraiḥ' is 'with sweet (ones)'; the noun is not given.
lines_deva: पिच्छिलश्च हितो बस्तिः स्नेहश्च मधुरैः शृतः
lines_iast: picchilaśca hito bastiḥ snehaśca madhuraiḥ śṛtaḥ

hindi: क्षार, खट्टी, तीक्ष्ण, गर्म और नमकीन बस्ति, या पित्त वाले की
english: A basti (enema) that is kṣāra, sour, sharp, hot and salty, or (that) of (one) who is paittika (of Pitta),
notes: GROUPING: 105 to 108 appear to be one passage; the verb 'karoti' is in 106. The line is read 'a basti that is kṣāra, sour, sharp, hot and salty, or (given) to a paittika (Pitta-type) (one)'; the Sanskrit gives only the genitive 'paittikasya', so the translation keeps it as a genitive. kṣāra is kept as the Sanskrit word.

hindi: गुदा को जलाते, खुरचते और क्षति पहुँचाते हुए यह इसके लिए परिस्रव यानी बहाव कर देता है।
english: Burning, scraping and damaging the anus, it makes a flow (parisrava) for him.
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 105 (subject: the basti of 105). 'kṣiṇvan' (printed) is read as the present participle of √kṣi, 'damaging, wasting'; the exact sense is not certain.

hindi: जलने सहित रक्त बहता है, रंगों के साथ, और पित्त बहुत मात्रा में भी।
english: It discharges blood together with the burnt (vidagdha), with colours, and Pitta, abundantly.
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 106. 'savidagdham' is read with 'asram' (blood together with what is burnt); 'vidagdha' is not specified further (it can mean scorched, over-heated). 'varṇaiḥ' is plural, 'with colours'. Raktapitta-like bleeding is not named here. The reading is literal.
lines_deva: सविदग्धं स्त्रवत्यस्रं वर्णैः पित्तं च भूरिशः
lines_iast: savidagdhaṃ stravatyasraṃ varṇaiḥ pittaṃ ca bhūriśaḥ

hindi: और बहुत बार अत्यधिक वेग से वह मोह यानी मूर्च्छा को प्राप्त होता है, बार-बार।
english: And many times, with excessive urge (vega), (he) goes into moha (bewilderment, fainting), repeatedly.
notes: GROUPING: appears to end the passage 105 to 108. The subject of 'gacchati' (the patient) is not named. 'moha' is rendered bewilderment or fainting; the text gives only the word moha. Modern equivalent: fainting or loss of awareness (probable).

words.gloss: fresh, moist; śālmalī (printed 'śāmalī'; silk-cotton tree, Bombax ceiba; probable); tantra (thread, fibre; sense unclear here)

hindi: वहाँ अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार, कुचले हुए ताज़े शामली यानी सम्भवतः सेमल के तन्त्रों, जिनका अर्थ यहाँ अस्पष्ट है, से उबाला हुआ बकरी का दूध
english: In that (case), on a conjectural reading: goat's milk boiled with crushed, fresh śāmalī (probably śālmalī, the silk-cotton tree) tantra (threads, fibres; unclear),

text_flags.why: possible: 'śāmalī' for śālmalī (silk-cotton tree); 'tantra' is also doubtful and is not changed

notes: GROUPING: 109 and 110 appear to be one sentence; the verb is 'dadyāt' in 110. 'śāmalī' is not a known word; śālmalī (silk-cotton tree, Bombax ceiba; probable) is likely, with the l-m conjunct lost. 'tantra' (thread, fibre) as a plant part is unclear and is not enriched. The reading is conjectural.

hindi: छाना हुआ, घी से युक्त बस्ति दे, और अन्य चिपचिपों को भी।
english: Strained, joined with ghee, he should give a basti (enema), and other slimy (ones).
notes: GROUPING: appears to complete 109. The participles 'pūtam' and 'ghṛtānvitam' are neuter and agree with the milk (payaḥ) of 109. 'anyān ca picchilān' is read as other slimy (bastis); the noun is not stated, so 'bastis' is not added to the translation.

words.gloss: vaṭa (banyan, Ficus benghalensis; standard); and the rest; sprouts (pallava)

hindi: वट यानी बरगद आदि के कोंपलों में इसी प्रकार कल्प है, और यव तथा तिल में भी।
english: Thus is the kalpa (preparation) in the sprouts of vaṭa (banyan) and the rest, and in yava (barley) and tila (sesame).
notes: GROUPING: 111 and 112 appear to be one sentence ('śasyate' is in 112). 'vaṭādi' means vaṭa and the rest; the other members are not named in the text and none is supplied. 'evam kalpaḥ' is read as 'the preparation is thus', that is, as in 109 and 110; this is an inference from the context.

words.gloss: suvarcalā (disputed; sometimes read as hulhul, Cleome viscosa); upodakā (Malabar spinach, Basella alba; probable)
karbudāra (commonly a white-flowered form of kovidāra, Bauhinia variegata; disputed)

hindi: सुवर्चला यानी विवादित पहचान वाली, सम्भवतः हुलहुल और उपोदका यानी सम्भवतः पोई में, और कर्बुदार यानी सम्भवतः कचनार में प्रशस्त है।
english: It is recommended in suvarcalā (identity disputed; perhaps Cleome viscosa) and upodaka (probably Malabar spinach, Basella alba), and in karbudāra (probably Bauhinia variegata; disputed).
notes: GROUPING: appears to complete 111. Identifications: suvarcalā is disputed (hulhul is one view); upodakā = Basella (probable; printed 'upodaka'); karbudāra = kovidāra (Bauhinia variegata, disputed). The unstated subject of 'śasyate' is the kalpa of 111.

hindi: और गुदा में ठण्डे और मीठे सेक यानी धार से सींचना तथा लेप करे।
english: And in the anus, he should make cool and sweet pourings (seka) and coatings (pralepana).

text_flags.why: possible: accusative plural 'sekān' expected to agree with śītamadhurān and pralepanān

notes: The printed 'seka' is read as 'sekān' (accusative plural, agreeing with 'śītamadhurān' and 'pralepanān'); the final n is missing in the print. The noun after 'śīta-madhurān' is not stated; the two nouns 'seka' and 'pralepana' are taken as the objects. Alternative to the flag: the space in 'seka pralepanān' may be spurious, giving one compound sekapralepanān (pourings and coatings); the sense is the same.

words.gloss: rakta-pitta (raktapitta: a bleeding disorder, bleeding from the body openings; standard); atisāra (diarrhoea; standard); destroying

hindi: और यहाँ रक्तपित्त यानी रक्तस्राव का रोग तथा अतिसार यानी दस्त को नष्ट करने वाली क्रिया प्रशंसित है।
english: And here, the procedure (kriyā) that destroys raktapitta (a bleeding disorder) and atisāra (diarrhoea) is commended.
notes: The line is read as a single statement, 'the procedure that destroys raktapitta and atisāra is commended here'. Raktapitta is kept as the Sanskrit name; the modern equivalent given is a descriptive one (a disorder with bleeding), not a single named disease.

hindi: दाह आदि में त्रिवृत् यानी निशोथ का कल्क मृद्वीका यानी अंगूर के जल से पिए।
english: In dāha (burning) and the rest, he should drink a paste (kalka) of trivṛt (turpeth) with mṛdvīkā water (grape water).
notes: 'mṛdvīkāvāriṇā' is read as 'with the water of mṛdvīkā (grape)'; whether this means raisin water, grape juice or an infusion is not stated. 'dāhādiṣu' means dāha and the rest; the other members are not named.

hindi: वह तो पित्त, मल और वात को नष्ट करके दाह आदि को जीत लेता है।
english: That, indeed, having destroyed Pitta, faeces and Vāta, would conquer (those) beginning with burning (dāha).
notes: GROUPING: appears to explain 115. 'pittaśakṛdvātān' is a dvandva in the masculine accusative plural (the final member vāta is masculine; pitta is neuter). 'hatvā' is literally 'having killed'; here 'having destroyed'. It is possible that 'destroyed' means 'expelled', but the text says only hatvā.

hindi: और शुद्ध होकर शर्करा यानी चीनी से युक्त ठण्डी यवागू यानी पतली लपसी पिए।
english: And, purified, he should drink a cool yavāgū (thin gruel) joined with sugar (śarkarā).
notes: 'viśuddhaḥ' is 'purified' (the purging is understood from the context). 'śarkarā' is read as sugar, not gravel.

hindi: अथवा अत्यधिक विरेचन किए हुए और क्षीण मल वाले के लिए भोजन का प्रयोग करे।
english: Or he should employ food for (one) who is over-purged (and) whose stool is depleted.
notes: 'yuñjyāt' is read 'should employ'. The run-on 'ativiriktasyakṣīṇaviṭkasya' is read as two genitives (or one compound); the sense is the same. The two members are of the same person.

words.gloss: māṣa (black gram, Vigna mungo; standard); soup (yūṣa)
kulmāṣa (a preparation of partly cooked grain; probable)

hindi: माष यानी उड़द के यूष के साथ कुल्माष यानी सम्भवतः अधपका अन्न; पीने के लिए दही अथवा सुरा यानी एक नशीला पेय।
english: Kulmāṣa (probably a preparation of partly cooked grain) with māṣa (black gram) soup (yūṣa); as drink, curd or else surā (an intoxicating drink).
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 118 ('bhojanam'). Kulmāṣa is read as a preparation of partly cooked grain (probable); the exact sense differs between authors. The verb 'yuñjyāt' is carried over from 118 and is not supplied.

words.gloss: would pass (lit. would be made to sit [to evacuate])

hindi: जो पीड़ा वाला, अरुचि सहित, कच्चा और सड़ा हुआ त्याग करे
english: He who, in pain and with aruci (distaste for food), would pass raw, putrid (kuṇapa) (ones),
notes: GROUPING: 120 to 122 appear to be one sentence (the treatment is in 121). 'upaveśyeta' (to go to stool) is read as passing; the noun it governs is not stated, so the English supplies only '(ones)'; the Hindi keeps only the adjectives. 'kuṇapa' is rendered putrid (foul-smelling); the lexical sense is corpse.

words.gloss: ghana (probably musta, nut-grass, Cyperus rotundus; probable; lit. 'cloud')
kuṣṭha (costus, Saussurea costus; standard; here a drug name)
unclear (printed 'nadāru'; not a known drug name; possibly a damaged 'dāru')

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार, घन यानी सम्भवतः नागरमोथा, अतिविषा यानी अतीस, कुष्ठ यानी कूठ, नदारु, जिसका अर्थ अस्पष्ट है, और वचा यानी बच के साथ पिए।
english: On a conjectural reading: he should drink (them) together with ghana (probably musta), ativiṣā (Aconitum heterophyllum), kuṣṭha (costus), nadāru (unclear) and vacā (sweet flag).

text_flags.why: possible: 'nadāru' is unknown; a stray 'na' (or a damaged 'dāru') is suspected; not applied

notes: GROUPING: appears to complete 120. The compound is a dvandva with 'sa' (together with). 'nadāru' is not a known drug name; it may be a damaged 'dāru' (or a stray 'na' before it); no reading is applied. Which preparation is drunk (powder, decoction) is not stated. 'kuṣṭha' here is the drug, not the disease.

words.gloss: is made to flow out (is purged)

hindi: जिसके मल, वात, रक्त, पित्त अथवा कफ का अतिसरण कराया जाता है,
english: (He) who is made to flow out faeces, Vāta, blood, Pitta or Kapha,

text_flags.why: possible: 'q' for kṛ and 't' for s in 'matṛk' (asṛk); the sense (faeces, Vāta, blood, Pitta) fits

notes: GROUPING: appears to complete 120 and 121 as a list of what flows out; the treatment continues in 123. The print is corrupt: see text_flags; the intended words are read as śakṛt, vātam, asṛk, pittam. The Hindi keeps the sense 'whose ... is made to flow out'.

hindi: पक्व; वहाँ अपने वर्ग का बस्ति श्रेष्ठ है, वैद्य के द्वारा जीता गया।
english: Cooked (pakva); in that (case), a basti of its own group (svavargīya) is best, (what is) conquered by the physician (bhiṣagjita).
notes: GROUPING: unclear; 'pakvam' may belong to the end of 122 or begin a new statement, and the unit may continue in the next chunk. 'pakvam' (cooked or ripe) has no stated noun and no sense is applied. 'svavargīya' is 'belonging to its own group' (the group of drugs for the same condition is not stated). 'bhiṣagjitam' is read 'conquered by the physician' (the alternative is 'the physician's victory'); the neuter 'śreṣṭham' with the masculine 'bastiḥ' is also loose. Possible link with the next chunk: unit 124 begins 'ṣaṇṇām eṣām dvisaṃsargāt triṃśad bhedāḥ' (of these six, thirty by pairing); unit 122 lists five items (śakṛt, vāta, asṛk, pitta, kapha), so 'pakvam' may be a sixth item of that list. This is an inference, not a decision.
lines_deva: पक्वं तत्र स्ववर्गीयो बस्तिः श्रेष्ठं भिषग्जितं
lines_iast: pakvaṃ tatra svavargīyo bastiḥ śreṣṭhaṃ bhiṣagjitaṃ
